added_models.model: Inhaled allergen challenge in mild atopic asthmatics (late asthmatic response)

efficacy.population: Mild atopic asthmatics (allergen challenge); unselected asthma (trials)
efficacy.note: Members were tested on the late asthmatic response to inhaled allergen in mild atopic asthmatics: MK-1029 from 2011, setipiprant published 2014.
efficacy.quote: A Two-part Study of the Effects of MK-1029 in Allergen-Challenged Asthmatics (MK-1029-003)
efficacy.confidence_note: Opening year is the registry start of NCT01343407 (2011-04-19); the setipiprant challenge (Diamant 2014) is not registered and may be earlier.
efficacy.judgement: Opening untested entry at the earliest dated member use of the allergen challenge model; proxy year from the registry start date.

efficacy.population: Mild atopic asthmatics (allergen challenge); unselected asthma (trials)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: model: setipiprant cut late-response FEV1 AUC 25.6% vs placebo; trial: AZD1981 pre-bronchodilator FEV1 +0.02 L vs placebo, P=0.58
efficacy.note: Setipiprant cut the allergen late asthmatic response 25.6%, predicting a lung-function benefit; AZD1981, a member, had already missed its FEV1 primary in 1,140 asthmatics.
efficacy.short: Challenge said yes; FEV1 trials missed
efficacy.quote: However, the improvement for the highest AZD1981 dose (400 mg BID) vs placebo was not statistically significant (0.02 L, P=0.58), preventing interpretation of statistical testing for the lower doses.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers. Model side: Diamant 2014 (PMID 24964348, entrez 2014-06-26): 'setipiprant significantly reduced the allergen-induced late asthmatic response (LAR), inhibiting the area under the response vs. time curve (AUC(3-10 h)) by on average 25.6% (P = 0.006)'. AZD1981 was never run in the challenge model.
efficacy.reason: Challenge positive, member FEV1 trials failed
efficacy.judgement: Paired, not stated: no source sets the challenge result beside a member's trial. Dated 2014, when the model side became public (the AZD1981 registry result was posted 2013-09-10). Sibling-drug pairing as in the main strip. MK-1029's own challenge (NCT01343407, posted 2019-02-08) cut LAR FEV1 AUC to 0.48x placebo; its phase 2 FEV1 primaries split (NCT02720081 +0.107 L, p=0.023; NCT01624974 +0.047 L, p=0.28) and the program stopped. Not scored neg: no source states a class LAR bar.

patient_trials.quote: Although neither trial showed a statistically significant reduction in asthma exacerbations after adjusting for multiple testing, consistent and modest reductions in exacerbations rates were observed in both studies with the 450 mg dose of fevipiprant.
Although GB001 did not significantly reduce the odds of asthma worsening, reductions favoring GB001 were observed.

considered_not_added: OC000459 (timapiprant) allergen challenge (Singh 2013, ERJ): not a member drug of this class table; the member-drug challenges (setipiprant, MK-1029) are used instead.
Sheep Ascaris model (Shichijo 2009): the drug, S-5751, is a DP1 antagonist, outside the class.
Guinea pig models used for AZD1981 (Schmidt 2013): a rodent allergic airway model, same system as the draft's rodent-allergic-airway track.
Fevipiprant physiologically based biopharmaceutics model (2023) and population PK (2021): formulation and PK, run after phase 3; no efficacy or dose-to-response comparison.
QSP / in-silico dose-selection model: none found for any member.
PTGDR polymorphism studies (meta-analysis 2013): PTGDR is DP1, not PTGDR2; no genotype-to-drug-response comparison.
Patient ex-vivo cells or biomarker-selected responders: no source found that used patient cells to predict member-drug response; eosinophil-high subgroups are a biomarker, not a model system.

Allergen challenge for engagement/dose: challenge sputum eosinophils are themselves a human readout; MK-1029 challenge doses (60 and 500 mg) not stated as the basis of phase 2 doses, so no dose entry.
Allergic rhinitis allergen chambers / seasonal AR trials (BI 671800, setipiprant): a different indication with no stated asthma prediction.
Ullah 2024 mouse chronic asthma with rhinovirus on steroid: already in the draft.
